_comment: BENCHMARK INPUTS, SNAPSHOTTED BY IDENTITY AND NOT BY COPY.
sources/scope.md, 'Snapshots are append-only': each release archives the register state and
every fetched source version under a dated path with a SHA-256 manifest, and a prior entry is
never overwritten. The two benchmark inputs are held to that rule with one difference, and the
difference is a licence rather than a preference: THE BYTES ARE NOT ARCHIVED. The content of
both files is the IEA's Hydrogen Projects Database — directly in one case, quality-checked by
Odenweller and Ueckerdt in the other — and this repository is not licensed to redistribute it.
SO WHAT IS ARCHIVED IS THE IDENTITY: the publisher's URL, the day it was fetched, the size and
the SHA-256. That is enough for anybody to fetch the same file from the publisher and prove it
is the one these numbers were computed from, which is the whole purpose the snapshot rule
serves — 'the archive is what makes every published number reconstructible after the register
has moved on'. A hash does that without holding a copy nobody may pass on.
APPEND-ONLY, LIKE THE SNAPSHOTS. A refreshed benchmark is a NEW entry with a new date and a new
hash; the old one stays, because the counts in sources/hydrogen_docket.md and in pull request
#52 were computed against it and a reader checking them a year from now needs to know which
file they are about. sources/report_benchmark_gap.py verifies the live cache against the newest
entry per benchmark and says so on every run.
ONE BENCHMARK IN TWO VINTAGES, NOT TWO BENCHMARKS. Recorded 11 September 2026, after the
admission search made the relationship impossible to keep ignoring. Odenweller & Ueckerdt
(2025) IS the IEA's October 2023 database, quality-checked, and it keeps the IEA's own
reference numbers: 35 of the 54 references the search settled exist in both files under the
same number, 29 of them under the same name. The register had been treating them as two
independent lists and reaching for a NAME STEM to join rows that shared an identifier all
along — which is how a machine guess got into a class as a verdict (D54).
WHAT FOLLOWS FROM THE DEPENDENCY. The two files cannot be summed, cannot corroborate each
other, and a gap in one is not independent evidence of a gap in the other. What the older
vintage CAN do, and what it is now read for, is DRIFT: which entries left the list between
October 2023 and now, which were renamed, which are new. A project that vanishes from a
database is a project whose failure nobody counts (rule 17), and drift is the only place
that fact can be seen.
BRIEF 8 ADDS THREE SECTORS, AND EACH PUBLISHER'S LICENCE IS READ BEFORE ITS SNAPSHOT.
The rule above -- identity, not copy -- was written for two files nobody here may
redistribute. Brief 8's inputs are not all like that, so each snapshot below carries a
`licence` block saying what was read, where, and what it permits. A snapshot taken
without that block would be a snapshot somebody assumed was allowed.
SECTOR 2 AND 3 LICENCES, READ 12-13 SEPTEMBER 2026, BEFORE ANY SNAPSHOT AND WITHOUT ONE.
The three lists the cement/CCS and steel censuses are measured against are each behind an
affirmative acceptance -- an account login, a click-through, a registration form -- and
none of them was passed. What is recorded below is the LICENCE ONLY: no bytes, no hash,
no entry in `snapshots`, because nothing was fetched. `pending_snapshots` names what is
awaited and at what path it will land.
THE IEA CCUS DATABASE IS DESCRIBED TWO WAYS BY ITS OWN PUBLISHER and both are recorded
rather than reconciled. The product page for this very file states 'Licence CC BY 4.0'
and prints a CC BY citation string for it; the general Terms and Conditions exclude
'Standalone datasets, data explorers and databases' from the CC BY 4.0 Open Use Terms.
This register does not decide between two statements by one speaker -- that is a
disagreement, and it is held as one. IT DOES NOT NEED TO DECIDE: a hash-referenced
snapshot redistributes nothing and requires no transfer of rights, so it is permitted
under the stricter reading as well as the looser one, and the stricter reading is what
this register works to.

vintages.note: The live endpoint. The current vintage and the one the register measures against.

The IEA's October 2023 database, quality-checked, under the IEA's own reference numbering. NOT AN INDEPENDENT BENCHMARK: it cannot corroborate the live file because it is the live file's own past. It is read for drift between the two vintages and for nothing else.
The current vintage of T&E's own list and the one the gap is measured against.
The same list fourteen months earlier. NOT AN INDEPENDENT BENCHMARK -- it is the 2024 list's own past, on the same method, so it cannot corroborate it. Read for drift and for nothing else.

second_list.note: Independent of T&E: different authors, different method (official announcements compiled by PEM at RWTH Aachen), different vintage. This is the list drift is measured against, in the sense the brief asks for -- what one list holds that the other does not.

transport_environment.robots: robots.txt allows User-agent: * outside /cpresources/, /vendor/, /.env and /cache/, and disallows GPTBot and Google-Extended by name. The declared reader is neither of those and is not a training crawler; it is recorded here because a publisher that names AI crawlers has said something, and a reader that ignored it would be deciding on the publisher's behalf.
transport_environment.what_this_pass_does: Reads the two reports at reading pace with the declared reader, holds them in sources/cache/batteries/ which is not committed, and cites every entry by T&E's own chart label. ND is why no derived chart is published and NC is why nothing is sold; neither bites on reading a list and counting against it.

iea_ccus_projects_database.held: NOT RECONCILED, AND IT DOES NOT HAVE TO BE. A hash-referenced snapshot redistributes nothing and needs no grant of rights, so it is permitted on either reading. This register works to the stricter one: the bytes stay out of the repository, entries are cited by the publisher's own identifier, and sources/cache/ccs/ is gitignored except its index.
iea_ccus_projects_database.barrier: ACCOUNT LOGIN. The file is 'IEA CCUS Projects Database 2026.xlsx', updated 27/03/2026, and the product page answers 'You are either not logged in or your login session has expired, please login again or create an IEA account to download data.' No open route exists: api.iea.org/ccus answers 200 but is the CCUS LEGAL AND REGULATORY database (89 rows, keys Base legislation / Description / Issue / Link / Region / Regulation or law), not the projects database; api.iea.org/ccus/projects, /ccus/project, /ccusprojects, /ccus/projects-database and /ccus-projects-database/ccus all answer 404; api.iea.org/sdmx/dataflow answers 404 and sdmx.iea.org and data.iea.org do not resolve. THE BARRIER IS AN ACCEPTANCE, NOT A PROHIBITION, and accepting an account agreement is the account holder's to give.

global_ccs_institute.verbatim: Content: All content (including data, text, video, images, audio, and other material) accessible on the Website… 5. Intellectual Property Rights — Content. All intellectual property rights in Content (other than your Contributions) are owned or licensed by the Global CCS Institute. Nothing transfers to you.
global_ccs_institute.held: ALL RIGHTS RESERVED, AND COMPATIBLE WITH WHAT THIS PASS DOES. Nothing transfers, and nothing needs to: a hash-referenced snapshot holds an identity rather than a copy, and entries are cited by the publisher's own identifier. Nothing is redistributed.
global_ccs_institute.barrier: CLICK-THROUGH, THEN AN EMBED WITH NO DATA BEHIND IT. co2re.co/FacilityData presents a modal — 'Check here to indicate that you have read and agree to the Terms and Data Use Policy' — and the table itself is an app.powerbi.com embed. The page carries no .json, .csv or .xlsx URL and no /api path. Both the 'Terms' and the 'Data Use Policy' links point at the same Terms of Use page quoted above, which WAS read. THE BARRIER IS THE ACCEPTANCE AND THE EMBED, not the terms.

gem_global_iron_steel_tracker.verbatim: The recommended citation is 'Global Iron and Steel Tracker, Global Energy Monitor, June 2026 (V1) release.'
gem_global_iron_steel_tracker.held: THE BRIEF RECORDS GEM AS CC BY AND THIS PASS COULD NOT CONFIRM IT FROM THE PAGE IT READ. The tracker page states a recommended citation and no licence; the licence is not quoted here because it was not read. It is recorded as outstanding rather than assumed, and the bytes stay out of the repository either way on the hydrogen and batteries precedent.
gem_global_iron_steel_tracker.barrier: REGISTRATION FORM. The Global Steel Plant Tracker is now the GLOBAL IRON AND STEEL TRACKER (GIST), June 2026 (V1) release. /projects/global-iron-steel-tracker/download-data/ redirects to the tracker page, where the download sits behind a form at the #download anchor with no direct file URL in the markup.
gem_global_iron_steel_tracker.note_for_the_pass: THE NAME CHANGED AND THE BRIEF'S NAME IS THE OLD ONE. Brief 8 names 'GEM's Global Steel Plant Tracker'. Recorded here so the steel census does not silently measure itself against a differently scoped list under the brief's name.

pending_snapshots._comment: AWAITED, NOT FETCHED. Each of these is a benchmark this register is measured against and cannot reach: the barrier is an acceptance a person gives, not a term that forbids the snapshot. NO ENTRY IS ADDED TO `snapshots` UNTIL THE BYTES EXIST AND ARE HASHED — a snapshot is an identity, and an identity of a file nobody has is nothing. The queue with exact URLs and drop paths is in sources/manual/MANIFEST.json under `wanted`.
